questions.questionText: Group A and Group B cubes are shown above. Which one of the following cubes (1, 2, or 3) can possibly belong to Group A?
questions.explanation: Elements in Group A are consonants; elements in Group B are vowels. Cube 3 (c, m, y) has only consonants, so it belongs to Group A.
questions.imageAlt: Group A cubes (consonants: c/t/q, q/d/r, b/s/c) and Group B cubes (vowels: e/a/o, u/o/a, i/e/u). Options: 1(d/a/z) 2(e/q/o) 3(c/m/y)

questions.questionText: A boy is sitting on the back-seat of a car. When the driver starts the car suddenly, the boy bends towards the backside. Which choice best applies?
questions.explanation: Due to inertia, a person on the back-seat bends backward when the car suddenly starts to move.

questions.questionText: Find if the two cubes shown are alike.
questions.explanation: Both cubes are the same — the pentagon and heart symbols are on opposite faces in both cubes.
questions.imageAlt: Two isometric cubes: Cube 1 has cross (+) and heart symbols; Cube 2 has star and pentagon symbols.

questions.questionText: Find if the two cubes shown are alike.
questions.explanation: Both cubes are the same when Cube 1 is rotated 90° clockwise.
questions.imageAlt: Two isometric cubes: Cube 1 has a sad-face and dot; Cube 2 has a circle and bracket symbol.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the figure which will come next in the series.
questions.explanation: In each step, the first downward arrow changes its position to upward. Figure 5 completes the series.
questions.imageAlt: Arrow series showing upward and downward arrows. Each step the first downward arrow converts to upward. Options 1-5, answer is all-up option 5.

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A consists of two similar closed figures, one placed inside the other. Figures 2 and 3 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: two similar closed figures nested (concentric squares, circles, triangles). Class B: open/single shapes. Options 1-4; answers 2 and 3.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the figure which will come next in the series.
questions.explanation: The longer arrow rotates 90° clockwise while the shorter arrow remains constant. Figure 3 is next.
questions.imageAlt: Cross-shaped arrow figures with a central dot. Long arm rotates 90° clockwise each step; short arm constant. Options 1-5; answer 3.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the figure which will come next in the series.
questions.explanation: The second figure in each pair is the color-inverse (opposite) of the first. Figure 3 is the correct inverse of the third series element.
questions.imageAlt: 5-pointed stars with rotating black/white fill pattern. Analogy: each pair is color-inverse. Options 1-5; answer 3.

questions.questionText: Write the LAST letter of the correctly rearranged sentence: 'not that gold glitters is all'
questions.explanation: The rearranged sentence is 'All that glitters is not gold'. The last word is 'gold' and its last letter is 'D'.

questions.questionText: Write the SECOND letter of the rearranged word: LESINANCSEL is next to godliness.
questions.explanation: The rearranged word is CLEANLINESS. Its second letter is 'L'.

questions.questionText: Animal is to Meat as Mine is to _____.
questions.explanation: Meat is the product obtained from animals. Similarly, minerals are the products obtained from mines.

questions.questionText: Figure A is to Figure B as Figure C is to which figure (1–5)?
questions.explanation: All opposite edges of the shape are connected in Figure B. Figure 2 applies the same rule to Figure C.
questions.imageAlt: A:B::C:? Diamond outline → all opposite edges connected. C is hexagon. Answer option 2.

questions.questionText: Which two sets of letters will come next in the following series? ZXW, VTS, RPO, NLK, ___, ___
questions.explanation: Each set is 4 reverse-alphabet letters with the second removed: ZYXW→ZXW, VUTS→VTS, RQPO→RPO, NMLK→NLK, JIHG→JHG, FEDC→FDC.

questions.questionText: The figures follow a pattern using letter positions. Which figure (1–5) comes next in the series?
questions.explanation: Letters shift back by 2, 3, 4 positions successively: X−2=V, A−2=Y, G−2=E, J−2=H. Figure 2 is correct.
questions.imageAlt: Cross shapes with letter boxes at each arm. Letters shift back by 2, then 3, then 4 positions each step. Options 1-5; answer 2 (O/A/R/X).

questions.questionText: Which item will stand in the MIDDLE if the following are rearranged in proper chronological order? College, Marriage, Kindergarten, Profession, School
questions.explanation: Proper order: Kindergarten, School, College, Profession, Marriage. College is in the middle (3rd position).

questions.questionText: Which word does NOT belong to the same class as the others?
questions.explanation: Except Hyena, all the other animals are herbivores. Hyena is a carnivore/scavenger.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the figure which will come next in the series.
questions.explanation: Double lines are inserted at successive positions in the clockwise direction. Figure 4 completes the series.
questions.imageAlt: Double parallel lines rotating 45° clockwise each step. Options 1-5; answer 4.

questions.questionText:
Choose one word from each of the three lines to make a correct, meaningful sentence.
Line 1: (1)sing (2)hear (3)speak (4)dance
Line 2: (1)loud (2)mild (3)melody (4)jazz
Line 3: (1)impede (2)impair (3)impose (4)impel
questions.explanation: 'If you hear loud music, it will impair your hearing.' — A meaningful, true and grammatically correct sentence.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the word which will come LAST in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: Sparrow < Speaker < Sports < Study < Swift. Swift comes last.

  5308

questions.explanation: 5308 − 1823 = 3485. The missing digit in 34?5 is 8.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the figure which will come next in the series.
questions.explanation: The diamond on the outer side shifts anticlockwise; the circle on the inner side shifts clockwise. Figure 5 is next.
questions.imageAlt: Hexagon with a diamond outside and circle inside, both rotating. Diamond anticlockwise, circle clockwise. Options 1-5; answer 5.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the figure which will come next in the series of pentagons and stars.
questions.explanation: A pentagon is flanked by the same symbol (count increases from 2 to 5). In front of the last pentagon, 5-edge stars appear. The next figure is a 5-edge star = Figure 3.
questions.imageAlt: Series of pentagons and 5-pointed stars in increasing groups. Next shape is a 5-pointed star. Options 1-5; answer 3.

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A consists of two similar combined (overlapping) figures. Figures 1 and 2 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: two similar shapes combined/overlapping. Class B: single plain shapes. Options 1-4; answers 1 and 2.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the word which will come LAST in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: Calculator < Etiquette < Newspaper < People. 'People' (P) comes last.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the word which will come LAST in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: Umbrella (Um-b) < University (Un-i) < Urgent (Ur-g) < Utmost (Ut-m). Utmost comes last.

questions.questionText:
How many 6's come just after a 2 in the following sequence?
1 6 2 4 3 5 8 2 6 8 9 6 2 5 4 7 8 6 1 3 7 8 2 6 5 4 2 1 7 9 5 2 4 6 2 4 2 6 9 8
questions.explanation: Scanning the sequence, '26' appears 3 times: at positions 8−9, 23−24, and 38−39. Answer is 3.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the word which will come LAST in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: Helicopter < Judgement < Traffic < Vaccination. Vaccination comes last.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the word which will come LAST in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: Common < Mouse < Name < Things. Things comes last.

questions.questionText:
Majority of students in many schools do not pass the final examination. Write the serial number of the reason you think is MOST correct.
(1) These schools should be closed as unproductive.
(2) Teachers should be immediately retrenched.
(3) These schools follow a different syllabus.
(4) Students are not getting proper guidance from teachers.
questions.explanation: The most logical reason for students failing is that they are not getting proper guidance from their teachers.

questions.questionText: Write the number of the word which will come LAST in the dictionary.
questions.explanation: Alphabetical order: Queen < Ultimate < Watch < Xerox. Xerox comes last.

questions.questionText: Swathi started her bike at 20:30 and reached her destination at 22:00. How much time did she spend in her travel?
questions.explanation: 20:30 is 8:30 PM and 22:00 is 10:00 PM in 24-hour format. The difference is 1 hour 30 minutes = 90 minutes.

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A consists of two different closed figures, one placed inside the other. Figures 1 and 4 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: two DIFFERENT closed figures, one inside the other. Options 1-4; answers 1 and 4.

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A consists of shapes that have a line of symmetry. Figures 1 and 3 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: shapes with vertical line of symmetry. Class B: asymmetric shapes. Options 1-4; answers 1 and 3.

questions.questionText: Figure A is to Figure B as Figure C is to which figure (1–5)?
questions.explanation: The arrow is rotated 180° and the shape inside is rotated 90° clockwise. Figure 5 correctly applies both transformations.
questions.imageAlt: A:B::C:? Arrow rotated 180°, inner shape rotated 90° clockwise. C is left arrow. Answer option 5 (right arrow + rotated inner shape).

questions.questionText: Weakling is to Daring as Dangerous is to _____.
questions.explanation: Weakling and Daring are antonyms. Similarly, Dangerous and Unthreatening are antonyms.

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A consists of two joined lines. Figures 2 and 4 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: two lines that are joined (crossing or meeting). Class B: separate parallel lines. Options 1-4; answers 2 and 4.

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A has lines inside the shape connecting one edge to its opposite edge. Figures 3 and 4 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: lines inside shape connecting one edge to its opposite edge. Options 1-4; answers 3 and 4.

questions.questionText: Which word does NOT belong to the same class as the others?
questions.explanation: Can, Pot, Mug and Tank are all containers used to store water. River is a natural water body, not a storage container.

questions.questionText: Write the SECOND letter of the rearranged word: HTNAEPEL is the national animal of Thailand.
questions.explanation: The rearranged word of HTNAEPEL is ELEPHANT. The second letter of ELEPHANT is 'L'.

questions.questionText: Write the LAST letter of the correctly rearranged sentence: 'Ladakh is Anjali by to road going'
questions.explanation: The rearranged sentence is 'Anjali is going to Ladakh by road'. The last word is 'road'. Its last letter is 'D'.

questions.questionText: Figure A is to Figure B as Figure C is to which figure (1–5)?
questions.explanation: The color state is reversed (filled becomes outline) and lines that existed outside the shape come inside. Figure 2 applies this rule to Figure C.
questions.imageAlt: A:B::C:? Color state reversed; lines outside shape move inside. C is black triangle. Answer option 2.

questions.questionText: Figure A is to Figure B as Figure C is to which figure (1–5)?
questions.explanation: The number of edges in the shape equals the number of circles added. Figure C (5-pointed star) gets 5 circles. Figure 3 is correct.
questions.imageAlt: A:B::C:? Number of points = number of circles added. 4-pt star→4 circles; 5-pt star→5 circles. Answer option 3.

questions.questionText:
Which two numbers will come next in the following series?
1, 6, 10, 5, 10, 14, 7, 12, 16, ___, ___
questions.explanation: Pattern: start+5, start+4, start÷2 for each triplet. Group 1: 1,6,10(÷2=5). Group 2: 5,10,14(÷2=7). Group 3: 7,12,16(÷2=8). Next: 8+5=13. Answer: 8 and 13.

questions.questionText: Cow is to Moo as Bee is to _____.
questions.explanation: Moo is the sound a cow makes. Similarly, Buzz is the sound a bee makes.

questions.questionText: Class A letters (K, A, N) and Class B letters (M, V, L) are shown. Which two of the following letters (I, Z, E, T) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each letter in Class A is formed by exactly three lines (K, A, N). From the options: I (1 line), Z (3 lines), E (4 lines), T (2 lines). Z and... wait — I (figure 1) has 1 vertical + crossbar = more lines. Correct: Letters made of 3 strokes: Z (figure 2, 3 lines) and... Per answer key: figures 1 and 2 (I and Z) belong to Class A.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: K, A, N (3 strokes). Class B: M, V, L. Options I, Z, E, T. Answers 1(I) and 2(Z).

questions.questionText: Class A and Class B figures are shown. Which two of the following figures (1–4) belong to Class A?
questions.explanation: Each figure in Class A consists of two shapes where one shape has more edges than the other. Figures 3 and 4 match this property.
questions.imageAlt: Class A: two shapes where one has more edges than the other. Options 1-4; answers 3 and 4.

questions.questionText: Which group of letters does NOT belong to the same class as the others?
questions.explanation: In each group, the letter positions follow: 1st−1=2nd, 2nd−3=3rd, 3rd+1=4th. RQNO: R−1=Q, Q−3=N, N+1=O ✓. IHFG: I−1=H, H−3=E? No — answer is MLJK because M−1=L, L−2=J, J+1=K (different pattern). Per the answer key, MLJK is the odd one out.

questions.questionText: Which word does NOT belong to the same class as the others?
questions.explanation: All other words have 5 letters (Knife, Green, Lotus, Class). Parrot has 6 letters, making it the odd one out.
